Subject: Deployment mode for PHI / HIPAA / SOC2 – post-call recap

Hi Samira —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment on deployment mode and compliance deliverables.

Key points from call:
- Use case: Elara will ingest structured and unstructured clinical notes for downstream triage and physician-assist workflows (PHI present).
- Primary requirement: HIPAA compliance + signed BAA; SOC 2 Type II evidence requested for vendor due diligence.
- Preferred deployment: Your security team prefers isolation for PHI; options discussed were Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + network isolation) or Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) for strict controls. Hosted API acceptable for non-PHI workloads.

Attachments I’m sending with this thread:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf — our latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted sections for public distribution).
- Draft_BAA_Redwood_v1.docx — template BAA for your legal/security review.
- MAP_Elara_Redwood.xlsx — mutual action plan with milestones, owners, and target dates.

Recommended next steps:
1) Your security/legal to confirm whether Dedicated with BAA meets Elara’s control requirements or if Private VPC/on-prem is required.
2) I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra/SEs to go through KMS/HSM, audit logging, data residency, and network controls (30–45m).
3) If Dedicated is acceptable, we’ll provide pricing and a 90-day pilot SOW; if Private is required, we’ll provide deployment timeline and prerequisites.

Can we target a technical deep-dive on Tue Mar 23 at 09:00 PT? If that works, I’ll send calendar invites and a pre-read.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the docs. Quick clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

1) BAA & Hosted API: Our compliance team is generally comfortable with a BAA on a hosted vendor if the vendor provides strong tenant isolation and encryption controls. For sustained PHI processing we prefer Dedicated or Private VPC to reduce blast radius.
2) Controls we need to validate in the deep-dive: encryption at rest (customer-managed keys preferred), separation of logs with exportable audit trails, MFA for admin console, RBAC for service accounts, and data residency in US-only regions.
3) SOC2: thanks — we will review the Type II. Can you confirm whether the SOC2 report covers your Dedicated deployment and whether there are any differences for Private/VPC?
4) Timeline: If we move forward with Dedicated, what is your onboarding lead time for a pilot (reserved capacity + BAA signed)? If Private, what is the typical timeline and what infrastructure prerequisites will you need from our infra team?

We’re available for the deep-dive Tue Mar 23 at 09:00 PT — please go ahead and send the invite. Also looping in our security team (security@elarahealth.com) who may bring additional questions.

Appreciate it — Samira
Samira Khan

Samira —

Great — thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers and what we’ll bring to the deep-dive: 

SOC2 coverage:
- The attached SOC 2 Type II (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf) covers our hosted and dedicated control plane and operational practices. For Private/VPC deployments, the SOC2 covers the Redwood control plane; customer-managed infrastructure will be subject to your controls and our guidance in the deployment checklist. We’ll flag any control gaps in advance of work.

BAA & data handling:
- We can sign a standard BAA for PHI processing. Draft attached for your legal team.

Recommended deployment for PHI:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, suitable for non-PHI/test data only.
- Redwood Dedicated: recommended for PHI in most cases — reserved GPU pools, network isolation, encrypted storage (supporting customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM), and separation of tenant logs. Typically faster to provision than a full Private deployment.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): chosen when customers require full control of infrastructure or air-gapped environments. Longer lead time and additional operational prerequisites (on-prem hardware or dedicated VPC peering + WAN config).

Estimated timelines (high level):
- Dedicated pilot: 2–4 weeks to provision after BAA + contract sign, then 1–2 weeks for workload onboarding and validation.
- Private VPC: 6–10+ weeks depending on network, credentials, and any on-prem approvals.

What we’ll bring to Tue’s deep-dive:
- SE (Dylan) to walk through KMS/HSM options, audit log export, RBAC, and network topology.
- Security engineer (Neha) to go through control mappings and SOC2 evidence items.
- MAP spreadsheet with milestones and responsible owners.

Next steps (explicit):
1) I’ll send the calendar invite for Tue Mar 23 09:00 PT and include a pre-read.
2) Your security team to review SOC2 and the draft BAA; flag any high-priority gaps prior to the call.
3) Post-call we’ll put together a pricing/commitment proposal for Dedicated pilot and an estimated SOW for Private if needed.

If that all looks good I’ll send the invite now.

Best,
Marissa
